rows.text_1::eng: Livestock includes domesticated animals raised for food, labor, and other agricultural products.
Livestock keeping is the practice of raising animals.
rows.image_text::eng:
Livestock kept are:

 Cattle, poultry, sheep, goats, pigs, rabbits, donkeys etc

rows.section_1_text::eng: You may have milk or animals but no reliable market.
rows.section_1_extra_text::eng: Add value to milk (e.g., by making mala or sour milk), which preserves the milk and increases income.
rows.section_2_text::eng: Animals get sick easily, leading to low production.
rows.section_2_extra_text::eng:
* Vaccinate early.
 * Deworm regularly.
 * Maintain hygiene to reduce infections.
 * Call a vet when needed. 
 * Isolate sick animals. 
 * Cull animals that cannot recover. 
 * Remove ticks by hand or spray using dips.
 * Use safe local herbs (e.g., aloe vera, blackjack and tithonia) 
 * Provide good feeding to boost immunity.

rows.section_1_extra_text::eng:
* Plant fodder like Brachiaria, Vetiver, and Napier.
 * Keep only the number of animals you can comfortably feed.
 * Prepare fermented feeds
rows.section_2_text::eng: Poor feeding and breeding affect growth.
rows.section_2_extra_text::eng:
* Use improved feeds for each growth stage.
* Monitor animals for disease signs.
* Observe breeding behavior (e.g., heat signs).

rows.section_1_text::eng: Animals may be stolen or attacked.
rows.section_1_extra_text::eng:
* Keep dogs
 * Fence the homestead.
 * Install security lights.
 * Build stronger livestock shelters.
 * Report issues through local authorities (chief, nyumba kumi).
rows.section_2_text::eng: Poor or weak animal shelters cause stress and disease.
rows.section_2_extra_text::eng:
* Build proper shade for animals.
 * Maintain good hygiene and sanitation.
 * Use simple portable structures (e.g., masera/otete for chicks)
 * Repair damaged shelters.

rows.section_1_text::eng: Lack of pasture and water causes poor animal nutrition.
rows.section_1_extra_text::eng:
* Store feeds early (e.g., hay). 
 * Dig a well or borehole for water.
 * Give mineral supplements (e.g., salt lick).
 * Plant more fodder crops.

rows.text_1::eng: Some ways of ensuring proper poultry health through general management practices and environmental sanitation are:
rows.section_1_text::eng: Keep vegetation short around poultry houses to reduce hiding spots for pests.
rows.section_2_text::eng: Clean houses regularly to prevent disease.

rows.media_transcript::eng:
Factors to consider when feeding livestock.

Breed or species:
Different animals, such as poultry, cows, and goats, require different types of feed.

Age:
Chicks, growers, layers, calves, and adult cows each have specific feeding requirements.

Production purpose:
Animals kept for meat production or egg production require different nutrients.

Health status:
Sick, pregnant, and breeding animals require special attention in feeding.

Sex:
Male animals generally consume more feed than females.

rows.section_1_text::eng: It includes preparing different types of livestock feeds at home using locally available farm and simple household materials, mainly aimed at reducing the cost of feeding livestock
rows.section_2_text::eng: Watch the videos in the 'Practical Section' on how to make these feeds and the ingredents used.

rows.text_1::eng: Fermented feeds are prepared without air (anaerobic conditions) using microorganisms. This process improves nutrient absorption and digestibility.
rows.image_text::eng:
We use locally available materials, following the Go–Grow–Glow ratio:
 * 70% Go (Carbohydrates)
 * 25% Grow (Proteins)
 * 5% Glow (Vitamins & Minerals)

Other useful additives… that can be included in fermented feed:

Cooked rice… for indigenous microbes.
Organic manure… used as a microbe starter.
Poultry microbes… or effective microorganisms.
Banana stems and leaves.
Weeds… such as blackjack, gallant soldier, and wandering jew.
Napier grass… arrowroot leaves… and pumpkin leaves.

Benefits of fermenting animal feed:

Improves birds’ gut health
Lowers feeding costs by using local materials and weeds.
Fermentation starts digestion… making feed easier to digest… and nutrients easier to absorb.
Adds probiotics that boost immunity.
Preserves feed during seasons of plenty… for use in dry periods.
Reduces anti-nutritional factors in certain ingredients — such as fodder trees and soya — thereby increasing nutrient availability.

rows.text_1::eng: It is feed you prepare yourself by mixing locally available ingredients to meet the nutritional needs of your animals

rows.media_transcript::eng:
Benefits of homemade feed:

Reduces feeding costs.
Uses locally available resources.
Allows farmers to control the quality of feed given to animals.

rows.text_1::eng: Silage making is the process of preserving fresh green plant material such as maize, sorghum, or grass by creating conditions that allow it to ferment naturally in the absence of air.
rows.image_text::eng: It is a method of preserving animal feed during seasons of plenty, so it can be used when feed is scarce.
